_doc: Resource model, PBS policy (derecho only) and pinned inputs for nudge_solver.gen_job, which writes a PBS wrapper around scripts/waxrun/nudge_gen.py (a Python port of the NCL Gen_Data_ne30 generator with identical output). Every wrapper ends with the validator, so a bad generation fails the job and the spinup that waits on it is held.
_measured: nudge_gen.py on Derecho: 11 s per 3-hour slot at --workers 1, 1.6 GB RSS per worker; the per-slot cost grows under concurrency (13.5 s at --workers 4), hence margin 2.0. ESMF_RegridWeightGen (--weights auto, cold cache) took 2.6 s; weights_gen_s is a generous allowance.
_limits: pbs.max_ncpus is the per-node core count (it refuses an over-large nudging.gen_workers); pbs.max_walltime_s is the generator job's walltime cap and decides how many days one chunk covers; pbs.max_mem_gb is a derecho node's usable memory.
_job_priority: pbs.job_priority true: the generator job carries the run's '-l job_priority=' (as CIME's case jobs on every derecho queue do); false for a queue that does not take it.
_tmpdir: {USER} is expanded at generation time, not by the job's shell: PBS exports LOGNAME, not USER, and $USER under set -u would abort the job.
_esmf: inputs.esmf_rwg is pinned and passed as --esmf-bin with --strict-esmf: ESMF 8.6.0 produces a slightly different weight set (223078 vs 223082 weights), which changes the outputs in the last float32 bit.
_modules: Empty: nudge_gen.py runs through the absolute interpreter baked into the wrapper and the pinned ESMF_RegridWeightGen, neither needs a module. Do not add esmf (another version changes the weights). A system whose interpreter is not self-contained can list modules here.
